title: Cassandra Wilson, Grammy-Winning Jazz Musician, Dies at 70
description:
Cassandra Wilson, the Grammy-winning jazz singer, songwriter and producer, has died. She was 70.

	Wilson’s longtime manager Robert Torre shared wit
body:
Cassandra Wilson, the Grammy-winning jazz singer, songwriter and producer, has died. She was 70.

	Wilson’s longtime manager Robert Torre shared with WBGO that Wilson died early Wednesday morning in Jackson, Mississippi. A cause of death was not given.

	“It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of Cassandra Wilson, the Grammy Award-winning and legendary jazz artist,” reads Torre’s statement. “Cassandra Wilson transitioned peacefully at home, surrounded by family, close friends, and her manager. Her family and close friends respectfully ask for privacy during this difficult time as they grieve her loss.”
	

	Throughout her career, Wilson was a relatively prolific jazz musician with an emotive contralto who incorporated elements of blues and funk into her songwriting. She won two Grammys, including the award for best jazz vocal performance in 1997 with “New Moon Daughter” and best jazz vocal album in 2009 with “Loverly,” and collaborated extensively with Steve Coleman as well as the Roots, Wynton Marsalis and Greg Osby. In 2001, Time magazine declared her “America’s Best Singer.”

	Born in Jackson, Mississippi, Coleman began playing piano at the age of six and picked up the guitar at 12, according to a bio on her website. She moved to New York City in the early 1980s and met saxophonist Coleman to found M-Base, a collective of musicians that also counted Geri Allen and Osby.

	She released her debut solo album “Point of View” in 1986 and followed with a string of projects before signing to Blue Note Records for 1993’s “Blue Light ‘Til Dawn,” hailed at the time for its blend of blues, jazz and pop but also considered controversial in the jazz world for skirting more traditional jazz conventions.
	

	Over the years, she continued to record and release albums of originals and covers of songs from Neil Young, Cyndi Lauper and Bob Dylan. She collaborated with numerous artists across genres including Luther Vandross, Angelique Kidjo, Terrence Blanchard and Olu Dara. She most recently released her final solo album “Coming Forth by Day” in 2015 as an homage to Billie Holiday.

schema.headline: Cassandra Wilson, Grammy-Winning Jazz Musician, Dies at 70

title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Shot Without a Finished Script, but Co-Director Joe Russo Says ‘We Always View’ the Screenplay as a ‘Living Organism’
description: “Avengers: Doomsday” going into production without a finished script did not faze directors Joe and Anthony Russo. As the former recently told the A
body:
“Avengers: Doomsday” going into production without a finished script did not faze directors Joe and Anthony Russo. As the former recently told the Associated Press: “We always view the script as a living organism.”

	“We’re improvisation-based, rehearsal-based directors,” Joe maintained. “We like to see what the actors bring to the characters, and sometimes you don’t get the actors until a few days or few weeks before you shoot them. And a lot of the time, that’s when the magic happens.”
	

	The Russo Brothers are making their grand return to Marvel with “Doomsday,” which marks their first MCU tentpole since the record-breaking “Avengers: Endgame.” The duo had not planned to come back for the next “Avengers” movie, which was originally going to be “The Kang Dynasty” and feature Jonathan Majors as the new Thanos-sized villain. But Majors got the boot from Marvel amid legal troubles, and the fifth “Avengers” movie had to be overhauled. That’s when the Russo Brothers stepped in alongside Robert Downey Jr., who is rejoining the MCU after the end of his Iron Man tenure to debut as the villainous Doctor Doom.


	“The thing that Joe and I have always appreciated about our collaboration with Marvel is: Our job isn’t to answer for the entirety of the MCU,” Anthony Russo told the AP about coming back. “We intersect it in a very specific way. It’s that intersection which is where we can make sense of things.”

	Marvel has a grand reputation for starting production on its movies without finished scripts. When “Guardians of the Galaxy” trilogy director James Gunn took over DC Studios, he vowed not to fall down this rabbit hole and only move into production on DC movies with finalized screenplays.
	

	“I do believe that the reason why the movie industry is dying is not because of people not wanting to see movies,” Gunn told Rolling Stone last year. “It’s not because of home screens getting so good. The number-one reason is because people are making movies without a finished screenplay.”

	Gunn noted at the time that DC Studios recently “killed a project” because the script just couldn’t get to the right place, explaining: “Everybody wanted to make the movie. It was greenlit, ready to go. The screenplay wasn’t ready. And I couldn’t do a movie where the screenplay’s not good.”

schema.headline: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Shot Without a Finished Script, but Co-Director Joe Russo Says ‘We Always View’ the Screenplay as a ‘Living Organism’

title: Carla Jeffery, Actress in Disney Channel’s ‘Zombies,’ Dies at 33
description:
Carla Jeffery, who played the cheerleader Bree in the Disney Channel’s 2018 movie “Zombies” and several spin-offs, died Sept. 1. She was 33.

	Her m
body:
Carla Jeffery, who played the cheerleader Bree in the Disney Channel’s 2018 movie “Zombies” and several spin-offs, died Sept. 1. She was 33.

	Her management company, Alexanders Talent, posted about her death on Instagram, but did not give a cause of death. 

	“For more than 20 years, Carla was part of the Alexanders Talent Management family, and watching her grow from a talented young girl into the beautiful, vibrant woman and actress she became was an incredible privilege,” said the agency. “We will remember her infectious smile, her laughter, her talent, and the beautiful light she carried everywhere she went.
	

	“Our deepest love and condolences are with Carla’s family and loved ones. We ask that their privacy be respected during this incredibly difficult time. Rest beautifully, Carla. You will be deeply missed and forever loved,” the statement continued.


	Jeffery played Bree in “Zombies 2” and “Zombies 3” and returned more recently to voice the character in “Zombies: The Re-Animated Series.”

	Before “Zombies,” Jeffery had small roles in shows including “Crazy Ex-Girlfriend,” “Uncle Buck” and “American Vandal.” She appeared as Keysha Black in 10 episodes of “Curb Your Enthusiasm” and played Janila on the police drama “Southland.”

	Born in Houston, she was the sister of actor Carlon Jeffery, who appeared in Disney Channel’s “A.N.T. Farm.”

schema.headline: Carla Jeffery, Actress in Disney Channel’s ‘Zombies,’ Dies at 33

title: Ryan Reynolds Praises ‘The Odyssey’ After Passing ‘Deadpool & Wolverine’ to Become Biggest R-Rated Movie Ever: ‘Christopher Nolan Literally Breathes The Rarest Air on Earth’
description: Hollywood is living through “the friggin’ salad days,” as Ryan Reynolds puts it, after experiencing the biggest summer at the box office since COVID
body:
Hollywood is living through “the friggin’ salad days,” as Ryan Reynolds puts it, after experiencing the biggest summer at the box office since COVID, thanks to blockbusters like “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey.” Last month, the “Deadpool” star personally congratulated the cast and crew of “The Odyssey” for surpassing “Deadpool & Wolverine” to become the highest-grossing R-rated movie of all time.
	

	“Obviously, [‘The Odyssey’] is an incredible, incredible movie. Christopher Nolan literally breathes the rarest air on Earth. He’s a singular filmmaker,” Reynolds told Variety at the “Mayday” premiere at AMC Lincoln Square in New York City on Tuesday night. “I mean, Matt Damon, Tom Holland, who’s clearly batting a thousand stars with Zendaya. I just love that people are going to the movie theaters. I don’t even care why or for what reason. Just go to the movie theaters. There’s no better shared experience.”


	Apple Original Films’ “Mayday” marks Reynolds’ first major movie role since “Deadpool & Wolverine” hit theaters more than two years ago. Set at the end of the Cold War, he stars as a U.S. Navy pilot who becomes trapped behind enemy lines and forms an unlikely friendship with an eccentric ex-KGB agent (Kenneth Branagh) who idolizes ’80s American culture. Reynolds believes that the rosy-colored nostalgia surrounding the decade, popularized in modern-day projects like “Stranger Things,” tends to gloss over the more turbulent nature of the era.

	“When you get far enough away from a time period that’s quite distinct, there’s always a lovely feeling associated with it, almost like you pave over all the trauma with puppy dogs and ice cream,” Reynolds said. “The 80s was a brutal, brutal time for people. It was a fucking mess and people forget that.”
	

	Reynolds was quick to point to the fear of nuclear war that lingered over Americans as U.S.-Soviet tensions surged again in the early ’80s. The decade also saw the decline of American manufacturing devastate many working-class communities, along with the AIDS epidemic, which became the country’s most urgent health crisis.

	“It was a tremendous strife,” Reynolds explained. “Socio political tensions everywhere. We were still pretty fresh off a Cuban missile crisis, which was only 15-20 years before. It’s a tumultuous period, but you look back at it now and you’re like, ‘Oh, yeah. ‘Top Gun.’ Cocaine!’ Like, ‘No!’ It was really scary.”

	When the time comes to dissect the 2020’s in decades to come, Reynolds predicts that creatives will “pick on the big ticket items that didn’t really leave the footprint culturally that you would think they would.”

	“So much of the aughts were like a mix of all the decade’s previous, whereas the decade’s previous were their own thing. I wonder if it’s going to be the Covid era or something. I have no idea. We are living in the friggin’ salad days right now! We just don’t know it.”

	While “Mayday” isn’t getting a theatrical release, Reynolds teased at this year’s San Diego Comic-Con that he could return as Deadpool later this year in Marvel’s “Avengers: Doomsday.” Reynolds snuck into the Marvel presentation at Hall-H in a grey denim Deadpool suit and asked Paul Rudd a question from the crowd: “Mr. Paul Rudd: where is Thor, and why was he crying?” 

	Branagh, who also directed the first “Thor” movie with Chris Hemsworth in 2011, says Reynolds never brought up the ongoing Thor gag while filming together on “Mayday.”

	“He worries about offending me, that’s what it is,” Branagh joked. “That was my baby, you know! Way back before you came in.”

	“Mayday” releases on Apple TV Sept. 4.

schema.headline: Ryan Reynolds Praises ‘The Odyssey’ After Passing ‘Deadpool & Wolverine’ to Become Biggest R-Rated Movie Ever: ‘Christopher Nolan Literally Breathes The Rarest Air on Earth’

title: Jenna Dewan Defends ‘DWTS’ Casting Amid Backlash: ‘Step Up’ Star and Ex-Janet Jackson Backup Dancer Says ‘I Do Not Know How to Ballroom Dance’
description: When the cast of “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 was announced on Wednesday morning, a few of the names raised eyebrows among fans of the reality
body:
When the cast of “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 was announced on Wednesday morning, a few of the names raised eyebrows among fans of the reality competition series.

	The most controversial casting, perhaps, is Jenna Dewan, a professional dancer who started her career as a backup dancer for Janet Jackson and starred opposite Channing Tatum in the 2006 dance movie “Step Up.” While the premise of “DWTS” is pairing professional dancers with celebrity amateurs, Dewan will be paired with a pro, ballroom expert and “DWTS” veteran Val Chmerkovskiy. Dewan’s casting sparked backlash online, with some fans arguing that Dewan has an extensive dance background and therefore has a clear advantage over the other contestants. Still, “DWTS” has no clear standard when it comes to the extent of contestants’ dance background, and many of the celebrities who have competed on the show have some experience.
	

	Dewan defended her casting in an interview with Entertainment Weekly, saying that while she is a highly experienced dancer, “I do not know how to ballroom dance.”


	“Let’s be clear. It’s two different languages,” Dewan told EW. “There’s parts of my dance training that’s helpful, obviously. I’ve learned choreography, I can perform, but there is a certain sense of unlearning for me. It’s a new technique, brand new technique. It almost threw me off initially because I had to unlearn a lot of — I don’t want to say bad habits — but just habits of the style that I’m used to.”

	Dewan said her dance background almost makes her “a little more nervous” to compete on the show, because ballroom “feels really foreign.” She explained, “It’s not like you’re giving me a style that I’ve done — I can go out there and do that. It has its advantages, but it also has its challenges. But that was part of why I wanted to do it. I really wanted to challenge myself.”
	

	Chmerkovskiy defended his partner’s casting, saying, “First of all, it’s naive to think that this show is just about dance. It’s about the human experience and the human journey and how much you’re willing to reveal yourself. Dance is a vehicle for us to find out more about these people — and I think that’s our advantage.”

	He conceded that Dewan “comes in with incredible talent,” but added, “with great talent comes incredible expectation — that’s my challenge.”

	“The way I approach things is that you’re only as good as the thing that you’ve never done, so I’m going to push her and push us to showcase to the world something they haven’t seen from her yet. That’s a challenge in itself because we’ve seen her at the highest form of dance and what that expression can look like —” Chmerkovskiy said, before Dewan interjected to add, “Many years ago!”

	The cast of “DWTS” Season 35 also includes Julia Stiles, Harry Shum Jr., Tatyana Ali, Tyler Cameron, Giada De Laurentiis, Maura Higgins, Ciara Miller, Taylor Hanson, Sarah Jane Nader, Guillermo Rodriguez, Jackson Olson, Ezra Frech, Amber Glenn, Conner Leavitt, and Connor Wood. 

	The series returns on Sept. 15 on ABC and Disney+.

schema.headline: Jenna Dewan Defends ‘DWTS’ Casting Amid Backlash: ‘Step Up’ Star and Ex-Janet Jackson Backup Dancer Says ‘I Do Not Know How to Ballroom Dance’

title: Tim Curry’s Cause of Death Revealed
description: A cause of death has been confirmed for “Rocky Horror Picture Show” star Tim Curry, a week after his death at 80. The actor’s main cause of death wa
body:
A cause of death has been confirmed for “Rocky Horror Picture Show” star Tim Curry, a week after his death at 80. The actor’s main cause of death was coronary artery disease, People magazine reported.

	The Los Angeles County Department of Public Health also listed a history of stroke and kidney cancer as contributing factors. 

	The theater and film star had suffered a near-fatal stroke in 2012. Doctors discovered two blood clots in his brain and performed emergency surgery. Following the stroke, the left side of his body was paralyzed and he required the use of a wheelchair.
	

	Curry was unable to speak for several weeks after the stroke. Although his voice returned the following year after rehabilitation, he focused mainly on voice acting for the remainder of his career.

	The actor was transparent about his stroke and recovery. “I still can’t walk, which is why I’m in this silly chair, and that’s very limiting,” he said at a 50th anniversary screening of “Rocky Horror Picture Show” in September 2025. “So I won’t be singing and I won’t be dancing very soon. I still have real problems with my left leg.”

	“I don’t fear death. I suspect that in the end I will welcome it,” he told Ben Mankiewicz last year. “I may well embrace it.”

	The actor’s last credited role was in the 2024 horror film “Stream.” He was set to return in an expanded role in “Stream 2: Sudden Death,” which is in production with Fuzz on the Lens Productions. The film will be dedicated to Curry, who completed filming his scenes for the sequel, director Michael Leavy said. 
	

	“I had been very scared when I did not know what was happening to me, because I had no sense of whether tremendous pain was forthcoming,” Curry wrote in his 2025 memoir “Vagabond.” “But if death comes for me peacefully and I fade gently from light into dark oblivion, why would I be afraid of it? Sometimes, I rather think it would be a comfort.”

schema.headline: Tim Curry’s Cause of Death Revealed

title: Jack O’Connell’s Ruthless Tabloid Editor in ‘Ink’ Fires Up Venice as Danny Boyle Drama Earns Warm 4-Minute Ovation
description: Venice Film Festival kicked off on Wednesday night with the splashy premiere of “Ink,” an explosive drama from director Danny Boyle about the rise o
body:
Venice Film Festival kicked off on Wednesday night with the splashy premiere of “Ink,” an explosive drama from director Danny Boyle about the rise of Rupert Murdoch’s tabloid empire.

	The film, which stars Jack O’Connell as The Sun editor Larry Lamb and Guy Pearce as media mogul Rupert Murdoch, was met with a short-but-sweet standing ovation of nearly four-and-a-half minutes. O’Connell appeared to joke about the marathon applause with Boyle, prompting laughs from co-stars Claire Foy and Pearce.
	

	It’s become customary for audiences at Venice to clap and cheer for seemingly forever after the credits roll at premieres. In the case of “Ink,” the hoopla may have been cut short because O’Connell and Claire Foy, who stars as a fictional journalist, began to walk back to their seats, collect their belongings and head for the exit. That’s after festival director Alberto Barbera tried to extend the clapping by telling the cast to move up on the stairs inside the Palazzo del Cinema, where the premiere was held. They obliged, but only for a few moments. 


	“Ink” premiered on Wednesday evening after a tribute to George Clooney, who was honored with a life achievement award. Clooney and his wife Amal walked the red carpet along with O’Connell, Pearce, Foy and Boyle. Other A-listers, like Jonathan Bailey, were also in attendance. They dutifully signed autographs and posed for selfies with the superfans (some of whom had camped out overnight for a prime spot in front of the red carpet) before heading into the Sala Grande Theatre. It was so hot and humid on Lido that O’Connell took off his Dunhill coat and handed it to a publicist before blotting the sweat on his face and white shirt with paper towels.
	

	Set in 1969 London, “Ink” follows a young Murdoch, who buys The Sun and transforms the struggling paper into a high-selling tabloid. O’Connell stars as “The Sun” editor Larry Lamb, Pearce portrays Murdoch, and Foy plays a fictional journalist named Jules Davies.

	Of course, Murdoch became one of the most influential — and divisive — media figures in history. The 95-year-old Australian built an empire spanning television, sports and entertainment through the conglomerate Fox Corporation, which includes Fox News and Fox Sports, as well as newspapers such as Wall Street Journal and New York Post. During Wednesday morning’s press conference for “Ink,” Boyle noted the movie doesn’t “monsterize” Murdoch, which he says, “a lot of people do now.”

	“He represented, at the time, a breath of fresh air in what was a very rigid British society,” Boyle said. “He offered a kind of freedom with a different voice.”

	“Ink,” which was acquired by Netflix prior to the festival, is competing for the Golden Lion. After Venice, the streamer will bring the awards hopeful to North America for stops at Telluride and Toronto International Film Festival. “Ink” will debut in theaters on Dec. 11 before landing on Netflix on Jan. 8.

	Venice is opening against a politically charged backdrop, and jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal spoke to tensions surrounding the wars in Gaza and Ukraine, as well as U.S. politics, at Wednesday morning’s press conference. She said she thinks movies are “fundamentally, unavoidably political,” adding that no subject should be off limits. “I think we can challenge ourselves to hear stories about the most corrupt, most perverse people because it opens up the opportunity to find empathy for those people.”

	Gyllenhaal also spoke about lack of female directors in this year’s competition lineup. Only two films up for the Golden Lion — “Woman Unknown,” a drama by Danish-Egyptian filmmaker May El-Toukhysolely and “Naza,” a documentary co-helmed by “No Other Land” filmmakers Rachel Szor and Yuval Abraham, were directed by women. 

	“There’s a systemic problem,” she said. “It’s harder for women to get films financed.”

schema.headline: Jack O’Connell’s Ruthless Tabloid Editor in ‘Ink’ Fires Up Venice as Danny Boyle Drama Earns Warm 4-Minute Ovation

title: New ‘Transformers’ Animated Short ‘Optimus Prime: Awakening’ Heads to Theaters – Film News in Brief
description: “The Transformers: The Movie” is returning to theaters internationally from Sept. 17 to 22 for the animated feature’s 40th anniversary. To celebrate
body:
“The Transformers: The Movie” is returning to theaters internationally from Sept. 17 to 22 for the animated feature’s 40th anniversary. To celebrate, there will be a new animated short “Optimus Prime: Awakening,” to play after the original 1986 film. 

	The 12-minute feature follows the original film’s storyline and serves as a “love letter to the ‘Transformers’ community and the late Peter Cullen,” Fathom Entertainment said in a statement. Cullen, who died on Aug. 26, delivers his final original voice performance as Optimus Prime and Frank Welker returns as Megatron/Soundwave. 
	

	“Optimus Prime and Megatron were made for each other.” Welker said in the statement. “After all, one needs the perfect hero against the epitome of evil to create great drama. Peter’s portrayal of Prime was born of his own personal beliefs; honesty, loyalty, and always insisting on doing the right thing.  This made it easy to be friends. Returning as Megatron and Soundwave for one final story opposite Peter’s Optimus in ‘Optimus Prime: Awakening’ was a real gift. I will miss my friend, but that voice and his heart and values will always be part of Optimus Prime.”


	The short and the anniversary screenings are presented by Hasbro and Fathom Entertainment. 
	
		WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 2	

	‘Fortitude’ Trailer: Spy Soldiers Fool Nazis in Action Film Based on WWII Deception

	Simon Afram Productions released the official trailer for “Fortitude,” an action-adventure film based on a real-life World War II operation.

	“Fortitude” follows spy-soldiers Dudley Clarke (Ed Skrein) and Thomas Argyll “TAR” Robertson (Matthew Goode) as they concoct a deception mission to fool Hitler and his army. The film is based on the real-life Operation Fortitude, an Allied military deception designed to fool Nazi Germany about the true location of the D-Day landing in 1944.
	

	Supporting the deception are Winston Churchill (Michael Sheen) and Ian Fleming (Art Malik), along with a network of double agents: the inspiration for the James Bond novels, Dusko Popov (Nicholas Cage), Spanish chicken farmer Juan Pujol (Jordia Mollà) and top British Intelligence agent Nancy Armstrong (Alice Eve).

	Simon West directed the film, which was written and produced by Simon Afram. Georgette Turner, Reza Roohi and Edward Kahl also produced. David Scaramanga, Bianca Goodloe, Daniel Haido, Blair Ward, Anders Erdén, Robert Leader, Joshua Levine, Abraham Taylor and Tom North served as executive producers.

	Watch the full trailer below.


	
		TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 1	

	‘George Michael: The Faith Tour’ Concert Film Releases Trailer

	A trailer for “George Michael: The Faith Tour” film debuts recently rediscovered footage from the star’s 1988 tour. 

	The concert film features never-before-seen footage shot on 35mm film. Over two nights at the Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy during the European leg of the Faith Tour, a 14-camera shoot captured Michael at the height of his fame amidst the promotion for his debut solo album “Faith.”

	“George Michael: The Faith Tour” is slated for a theatrical release on Dec. 11.

	The concert film was directed by Andy Morahan and David Austin. George Michael Entertainment and Mercury Studios produced.

	Watch the full trailer below.


	
		WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 2	

	Darran Tiernan and Steven Poster to be honored at Emerging Cinematographer Awards

	Darran Tiernan and Steven Poster will be honored by the International Cinematographers Guild at the 28th annual Emerging Cinematographer Awards (ECA) on Oct. 2.

	“Darran Tiernan’s innovative visual style and Steven Poster’s tireless advocacy for young filmmakers embody the spirit of excellence and leadership we strive to celebrate at the Emerging Cinematographer Awards,” co-chairs of the ECA committee Eduardo Fierro, SVC, and Amy Vincent, ASC, said in a statement. “It’s a privilege to recognize them both at this year’s awards ceremony.”

	Tiernan will receive the Distinguished Filmmaker Award for his visual storytelling on his latest project the Prime Video series “Spider-Noir.” His other titles include “The Penguin,” “Winning Time: The Rise of the Lakers Dynasty,” “Barry” and “Perry Mason.”
	

	Poster will receive the Mentor Award for his advocacy for film crews. Poster shot “Donnie Darko” and “Southland Tales,” along with “Rocky V,” “Amityville: The Awakening” and Madonna’s “Like A Prayer” music video.

title: Filmmaker Penny Lane Sets Documentary on Bronx Zoo Elephant, ‘Happy’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Documentary filmmaker Penny Lane (“Hail Satan?,” “Our Nixon”) has set her latest documentary on the Bronx Zoo elephant, Happy. The doc is being made
body:
Documentary filmmaker Penny Lane (“Hail Satan?,” “Our Nixon”) has set her latest documentary on the Bronx Zoo elephant, Happy. The doc is being made in partnership with Alex Gibney’s Jigsaw Productions and Sandbox Films.

	The untitled feature documentary reunites Lane with producers Gabriel Sedgwick and Julia Lewis, the creative team behind “Wild Inside,” the documentary focusing on Flaco the owl.


	Lane’s film is based on an article penned by Pulitzer Prize-winning historian Jill Lepore. Happy came to the U.S. from Thailand during the Vietnam War as an infant. Joining six other baby elephants at a Florida petting zoo, where each was named after one of Disney’s Seven Dwarfs, the untitled feature will explore the extraordinary lives of all seven elephants, covering a tumultuous 50-year period marked by changing perspectives on elephant care, management, cognition, and animal rights. Happy was euthanized on May 26 at the age of 55.
	

	Lane say, “Happy’s story, and the story of her six ‘siblings’, is a deeply fascinating journey through fifty years of human-elephant relationships in the United States, thousands of miles from any natural elephant habitat.” She adds, “Through this strange family saga spanning zoos, theme parks, circuses and sanctuaries, the film explores the complex intersection of science, conservation, capitalism, ethics, and law, and asks how our evolving understanding of elephants should change the way we coexist with them.”

	Happy gained recognition for passing the mirror self-recognition test, a feat that highlighted her advanced self-awareness. Later, Happy became the plaintiff in a landmark legal case arguing that her high degree of autonomy and intelligence warranted legal recognition as a “person.”
	

	Gibney says, “I’ve admired Penny’s work for years. She’s an incredibly original filmmaker with a real gift for finding surprising ways into complicated subjects. I’m excited to have the chance to collaborate with her, and with our partners at Sandbox, on this film.”

	In the process of making the film, the team is currently gathering memories, photos, videos, and stories from anyone who has encountered Happy and the six other Dwarf elephants. A timeline of the elephants’ known locations and name changes, along with information on how to submit materials, is available at elephantdocumentary.com. The material submitted doesn’t need to be professional quality to be valuable for the film or as historical documentation.Along with Gibney,  executive producers include Wendy Schmidt and Razan Ghalayini for Jigsaw Productions, Jessica Harrop for Sandbox Films, Julie Parker Benello for Secret Sauce Media, and Jill Lepore.

schema.headline: Filmmaker Penny Lane Sets Documentary on Bronx Zoo Elephant, ‘Happy’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Elliot Page Is ‘Not Really’ Getting Casting Calls After ‘The Odyssey’: ‘If Someone Wants to Call Me…I’d Love to Do Good Work’
description: Elliot Page has never felt more comfortable on screen. Finding the right role, however, has proven to be more difficult. During his appearance on th
body:
Elliot Page has never felt more comfortable on screen. Finding the right role, however, has proven to be more difficult. During his appearance on the “On Film… With Kevin McCarthy” podcast, Elliott revealed he hasn’t been able to find another great role after starring in “The Odyssey,” which hit theaters in July. The actor revealed he has no role currently lined up.

	The “Umbrella Academy” actor, who came out as transgender in 2020, said he hopes to continue acting. Looking back at his experience filming Christopher Nolan‘s 2010 film “Inception,” Page recalled feeling uncomfortable in his own skin. But now that he’s embraced his true identity, he feels he’s in the perfect place to accomplish his “best work.”
	

	“I had such a great time being in [“Inception”]. I had such a great time working with [writer-director Nolan], but I was also personally really uncomfortable,” the Oscar nominee shared. “Whereas a part like ‘Juno,’ I was able to feel more comfortable and embodied.”


	While working on Nolan’s film, Page developed shingles after feeling out of place while working “in a cast full of cis men.” In his memoir, “Pageboy,” the actor shared the cast and crew were “delightful to work with,” but he still struggled to feel comfortable on set. 

	Page reunited with Nolan for “The Odyssey,” which he told McCarthy was a “cathartic” experience compared to working on “Inception.” On his last day filming Nolan’s epic, Page said it was an emotional  day because it marked a full-circle moment. 

	“To come back now, as you can imagine, being more comfortable in yourself makes these sorts of projects more enjoyable,” Page said during the “X-Men: Days of Future Past” panel at New York City Comic Con in 2025 about “The Odyssey.” “To get to have a Chris Nolan experience again now meant so much to me selfishly.”
	

	When Page’s casting as Sinon, the cousin of Odysseus (Matt Damon), was announced, the actor faced backlash online. Conservative commentator Ben Shapiro called the choice an “absolute puzzler,” noting that Page is “about 5’2 and 105 pounds soaking wet and has the voice of a woman. It doesn’t work.”

	Whoopi Goldberg spoke out against Shapiro’s remark during an episode of “The View” in July, saying “A lot of conservatives who see this are going to feel the same way. That’s okay. But I don’t understand. Why go see the movie? If you don’t want to see it, don’t go see it. Why do you care who’s cast in it?”

schema.headline: Elliot Page Is ‘Not Really’ Getting Casting Calls After ‘The Odyssey’: ‘If Someone Wants to Call Me…I’d Love to Do Good Work’

description:

            Alphonso Smith Jr. -- a former NFL player and standout cornerback at Wake Forest University -- has died ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Sources with direct knowledge tell TMZ ... the former cornerback died by suicide on Wednesday at a housing community in Florida.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Alphonso's final Facebook post highlighted his unstable emotional state before his death.
      
    
            In the post, Alphonso wrote, "Do not cry for me! I tried everything in my power to fight the demons behind the ones that someone put into ME! I did not want to be that WAY! I know I have disappointed so many folks. This is a DEMON in me! But not only me! It’s EVERYONE! I have HURT so many! I needed help & did not get it!"
      

            He repeatedly apologizes in the post, calls himself a "coward" ... and includes a reference to some abuse suffered at the hands of an older woman when he was a young boy.
      
    
            Alphonso ended the post by writing, "I am SORRY! THIS IS IT!"
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Alphonso attended Wake Forest from 2004 to 2008 ... earning All-American honors in his final season with the school. He was inducted into the school's athletic hall of fame in 2022.
      
    
            He was drafted by the Denver Broncos in 2009 -- though they traded him to the Detroit Lions just one year later. He played 3 seasons in Detroit ... ending his career after the 2012 campaign. He recorded 88 tackles and 8 interceptions across 42 NFL games.
      
    
            Alphonso was 40 years old.
      
    
            RIP
      
    
            If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat 988lifeline.org.

                                                                Updated 
                                  September 2, 2026
                                2:34 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Tim Curry died from coronary artery disease, TMZ has confirmed.
      
    
            The Los Angeles County Department of Public Health made the determination -- first reported on by People -- that coronary artery disease was Tim's main cause of death. Kidney cancer and his history of strokes were listed as underlying causes.
      
    
            We broke the story ... Tim died at his Los Angeles-area home on Tuesday. Law enforcement sources told us no foul play was suspected.
      

            He dealt with health issues over the years ... most notably suffering a stroke back in 2012, which significantly decreased his mobility. He used a wheelchair through the rest of his life.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Tim -- best known for his roles in musical movies like "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" and "Annie" -- looked to be doing all right when a caregiver helped him into a North Hollywood pub in April, a few days after his 80th birthday.
      
    
            He was even working in the months before his death -- shooting all the scenes for the upcoming horror flick "STREAM 2: Sudden Death."
      
    
            Tim was 80 years old.
      
    
            RIP

title: 'All That' Star Christy Knowings Cause of Death Revealed
description:
'All That' Star Christy Knowings'
                          Cause of Death Revealed
body:
'All That' Star Christy Knowings'
                          Cause of Death Revealed
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 2, 2026
                            2:54 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Christy Knowings' cause of death has been revealed ... the former "All That" star died after suffering cardiac arrest ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to a death certificate obtained by PEOPLE, the certificate identifies asthma as the underlying cause, with status asthmaticus and acute hypoxic respiratory failure listed as contributing conditions.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            We broke the story ... Knowings was hospitalized in August after suffering an asthma attack that caused brain damage. A family member told us she was placed on life support, and her loved ones ultimately made the difficult decision to take her off it several days later.
      

      
        
              
    
    
            Knowings joined Nickelodeon's "All That" in 1997 after appearing in "And Now This," a Rosie O’Donnell sketch comedy special produced by the network.
      
    
            She spent three seasons on "All That," playing several characters, including Penny Lane and Jessica in the recurring "Whateverrr!!!" sketch alongside Amanda Bynes.
      
    
            Christy later appeared in three episodes of "Sesame Street" with her real-life twin brother, Chris Knowings. Christy was the second former "All That" cast member to die this year. As TMZ previously reported, Kianna Underwood was killed in a hit-and-run collision in Brooklyn in January.
      
    
            Christy was 46.
